correctness.rationale: PASS for the stated domain all integer d>=1 and q=3,4 (ordinary OPEN neighborhood). Distinct neighborhood simplices N(v), N(w) intersect in q-2 vertices at distance one, two at distance two, and none farther; since q<=4, every >=3-vertex face has a unique center. Fix anchor a_v in each N(v) and, in descending |sigma|>=3, remove each sigma subset N(v) minus anchor together with sigma+anchor. Any larger coface of the lower simplex lies in that same simplex and was already removed, so these are genuine elementary free-face removals on the ORIGINAL triangulation; only faces of dimension <=2 remain. When d(q-1)<4 no removal is necessary. The original graph is in the complex 1-skeleton, so connected. f0=q^d, f1=q^d/2 [d(q-1)+binom(d,2)(q-1)^2], and the unique-center contribution of size>=3 faces gives chi3=3^d(d-1)(d-2), chi4=4^(d-1)(9d^2-15d+8). Matsushita Thm1.1 and Behal-Chih Thm4.14 give pi1 and integral H1 via even-coordinate parity: Z^d for q3, (Z/2)^(d-1) for q4. Since the collapsed 2-complex has no 3-cells, H2 is a subgroup of free C2 and therefore free, with beta2=chi-1+beta1 as stated. d=1 boundary cases match K3 circle and K4 tetrahedral boundary. Independent checker reconstructed all faces and each elementary free-face incidence for seven (d,q) cases, specifically (1,3),(2,3),(3,3),(4,3),(1,4),(2,4),(3,4), with 432 pairs for (3,3), 8019 for (4,3), 256 for (2,4), 14016 for (3,4), and chi values 0,0,54,486,2,56,704; modular H1 ranks over F2,F3,F5 corroborate torsion. Symbolic Euler simplification checked independently. Finite checks are not a proof for all d, and the independent argument uses the identified primary group theorems.
residual_risks: Only 7 finite examples checked; all-d validity uses stated local intersection/free-coface argument and primary group theorems
No formal proof assistant or expert attestation is claimed

evidence: Every pair of distinct Hamming graph vertices has at most max(q-2,2)=2 common neighbors for q=3 or4; therefore all G_{d,q} are K_{2,3}-free. Kahle Lemma 2.3 applies for ALL d and already implies H_i=0 for i>2, with H2 torsion free as a subgroup of a free 2-chain group of its low-dimensional homotopy model.

Combining this with Matsushita and Behal–Chih first-homology input and the elementary closed-form Euler characteristic yields the entire displayed integral H2 rank formula; the homology classification is thus mathematically IMPLIED by prior general theorems plus standard counting, even without an earlier paper printing the formula.

The multinary Hamming scale-two Cech result concerns the nerve of closed radius-one balls, a different simplicial complex; its broader q-domain does not itself cover the original-face open-neighborhood collapse.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Decisive priority distinction: the all-d homology consequences are already available from Kahle+Matsushita+Behal–Chih and do NOT independently establish novelty. An explicit elementary collapse inside the original triangulation, preserving all original vertices and avoiding barycentric subdivision, remains a genuinely stronger combinatorial statement not supplied by the inspected broader theorem.

evidence: Kahle Lemma 2.3 proves a K_{2,3}-free graph has a neighborhood complex strongly deformation retracting to dimension at most 2, via the face-poset double-neighborhood map and its barycentric order complex. It does not assert an elementary collapse of the original unsubdivided simplicial complex.

Matsushita Theorem 1.1 relates fundamental groups of open-neighborhood complexes to the even subgroup of the 2-walk group; Behal–Chih Theorem 4.14 computes the Hamming graph groups. These cover fundamental groups and first homology.

Kozlov proves several simple-homotopy equivalences involving Hom and Lovasz neighborhood complexes, with barycentric subdivisions; not a uniform original-face elementary collapse to dimension 2 for the precise graph family.

The claimed group/H1 ingredients are expressly prior work.

value.rationale: PASS, qualified and narrow: a constructive ordinary elementary collapse of the ORIGINAL often high-dimensional Lovasz complex, without introducing barycentric vertices, is a mathematically natural stronger combinatorial reduction beyond the already-known abstract two-dimensional retraction. It supplies a uniform explicit sequence of free-face cancellations on a natural infinite family (both K3 and K4 Hamming powers), useful for chain-level models and reproducible simplicial calculations, not an arbitrary parameter slice. The H2 numbers and higher-vanishing themselves should NOT be advertised as previously unknown because a Kahle-based deduction already exists. This is a modest structural contribution rather than an independent new homology theorem or full homotopy classification.
residual_risks: Value is confined to stronger explicit original-face collapse, not the known homology implications or the existence of an abstract 2D deformation retract.

final_claim: For each d>=1, q in {3,4}, N(K_q^{square d}) admits an explicit ORIGINAL-triangulation simplicial collapse to dimension at most 2. It is connected, with H1=Z^d (q3) or (Z/2)^(d-1) (q4); H2=Z^{3^d(d-1)(d-2)+d-1} (q3) or Z^{4^(d-1)(9d²-15d+8)-1} (q4), and H_i=0 above 2. Algebraic homology formulas are already implicit in Kahle/Matsushita/Behal-Chih and only the constructive direct collapse is assessed as potentially original.
